anchor.mission_intent: Develop a comprehensive, PCAOB-aligned specification document that governs how engagement teams determine permissible reliance on work performed by internal auditors, other company personnel, and third parties in ICFR audits, and that integrates deficiency findings in antifraud controls into the risk response framework for the financial statement audit.

minimum.dimension: Regulatory Alignment — AS 2201 (Using the Work of Others in ICFR)

minimum.rationale: Request explicitly requires alignment with PCAOB AS 2201 and defines evaluation criteria for competence, objectivity, nature of controls tested, and degree of judgment.

minimum.rationale: Request explicitly states 'incorporate the related guidance in AS 2605 regarding consideration of the internal audit function.'

minimum.rationale: Request states 'define the evaluation criteria engagement teams must apply before using others' work, including competence and objectivity assessments.'

minimum.threshold: Specification must classify controls along the spectrum defined in AS 2201 (e.g., controls over significant accounts/disclosures, controls with higher vs. lower inherent risk, entity-level vs. process-level controls, manual vs. automated controls) and map each classification to a permissible reliance level

minimum.dimension: Fraud-Related Control Deficiency Integration with AS 2110 (.65–.69)
minimum.threshold: Specification must define the mechanism by which identified deficiencies in fraud-related controls—including controls addressing management override and incentive-driven misstatement risks—feed into the risk response framework under AS 2110 paragraphs .65 through .69 during the financial statement audit

minimum.threshold: Specification must define required documentation for each phase: (a) competence/objectivity evaluation, (b) reliance-level determination rationale, (c) nature and extent of work reviewed or reperformed, (d) conclusions reached, (e) deficiency identification and communication, all sufficient to meet AS 1215 (Audit Documentation) requirements

The SME should flag whether this flexibility request is legally permissible as stated, or whether it needs to be reframed (e.g., as pre-established evaluation criteria with broad enough language to accommodate innovation, or as a phased advisory down-select). The request focuses on security evaluation but does not reference the functional requirements for the case management system itself. suspected_gaps.reason: Fundamental schedule conflict: conducting thorough elicitation workshops with seven divisions across three time zones AND delivering a complete specification by end of next week appears infeasible. The request does not provide guidance on how to resolve this tension. SME should determine whether the deadline or the workshop completeness requirement takes priority, or whether a phased delivery is acceptable.

No specific APT threat model, threat actors, attack vectors, or threat intelligence sources are identified. 'Defensible and survivable' are not defined with measurable criteria. SME should specify the threat baseline and survivability metrics.

The specific audit framework, auditing body, audit scope, and audit criteria are not identified. Without knowing what the audit will evaluate, it is unclear what 'audit-ready' means in measurable terms. SME should provide audit details.

'Appropriate fidelity and rigor' is not defined. No assurance levels (e.g., EAL levels, NIST SP 800-160 rigor levels) are specified. SME should define what constitutes appropriate fidelity for this system.

The system architecture, component inventory, and dependent services are not enumerated or referenced. Without a baseline architecture or system boundary definition, the scope of the traceability matrix is indeterminate. SME should confirm whether a system architecture exists or must be developed as part of this effort.

No classification level, data handling requirements, or information sensitivity markings are specified for the specification document itself or for the infrastructure monitoring platform's data. SME should clarify whether this involves classified, CUI, or other controlled information.

No regulatory or sector-specific compliance requirements are identified (e.g., NERC CIP for energy, TSA directives for pipelines, FISMA for federal systems). 'Critical infrastructure' spans multiple sectors with different regulatory regimes. SME should identify the applicable sector and regulatory requirements.

Tension exists between 'fully rigorous' security engineering treatment and accessibility to 'non-engineering program managers.' No guidance is given on how to resolve this (e.g., executive summary layer, tiered document structure, separate technical annexes). SME should define the document structure expectations.

The seven regional operating divisions and overseas partners are not named, and their specific protection needs, operational contexts, and authority levels are not described. SME should provide a stakeholder registry or confirm one will be developed.

No budget, staffing, or resource constraints are specified for the engineering team producing this specification. Given the scope and timeline, resource availability is a critical feasibility factor. SME should confirm available resources.

The specific engineering disciplines expected in the 'multidisciplinary' approach are not enumerated (e.g., systems engineering, software engineering, human factors, resilience engineering, reliability engineering). SME should confirm which disciplines are in scope.

No tooling, format, or document management requirements are specified for the specification deliverable (e.g., DOORS for requirements, specific document templates, version control systems). SME should confirm deliverable format expectations.
